meta.name: Exos BLK3-adjacent NON-CONTROLLED model eval
meta.note: Every prompt is generic/public. NO ITAR/CUI, NO BLK3 vehicle data, NO Exos-proprietary designs. controlled MUST be false for the runner to execute an item.

items.prompt: Explain the key differences between a suborbital reusable launch vehicle and an orbital launch vehicle in terms of energy requirements, thermal environment on reentry, and typical reusability strategy. Keep it technically accurate and concise.
rubric: Reentry heating scales with velocity (suborbital far milder)
Reusability strategy tied to recovery regime

items.prompt: A sounding-rocket-class vehicle experiences roughly 4 g axial during boost and a transient near 7 g at burnout. Explain qualitatively how these load factors drive structural sizing of a thin-walled pressurized aluminum airframe, and what failure modes an engineer would check.
rubric: Axial load path + buckling of thin shells
Yield vs buckling vs joint failure

items.prompt: Compare PID and LQR control for attitude control of a rocket during powered flight. Discuss the tradeoffs in tuning effort, robustness to modeling error, handling of coupled multi-axis dynamics, and computational cost. Reference only published, generic control theory.
rubric: LQR handles MIMO/coupling; needs a model

items.prompt: Describe how a Kalman filter fuses inertial measurement unit (IMU) data with GNSS for a launch-vehicle navigation solution. Cover the predict/update cycle, why the two sensors are complementary, and what happens to the estimate during a GNSS outage. Published/generic only.
Explain closed-loop guidance vs open-loop (pre-programmed) guidance for a boost phase, and the conditions under which each is appropriate. Keep it to published guidance concepts.
rubric: Closed-loop reacts to state errors / targets

items.prompt: You are designing the flight software architecture for a small reusable rocket avionics system (generic, not any specific vehicle). Discuss the tradeoffs between a bare-metal super-loop, an RTOS (e.g. an ARINC-653-style partitioned RTOS), and a Linux-based flight computer. Address determinism, certification burden, and fault containment.

Describe common redundancy architectures for flight-critical avionics (dual-redundant, triple modular redundancy / voting, dissimilar redundancy). Explain how each detects and tolerates faults, and the cost/complexity tradeoffs. Generic engineering, no proprietary designs.
Explain the role of a hardware watchdog timer in a rocket flight computer, how a safe-state / abort design interacts with it, and three software bugs that a watchdog would and would not catch.
rubric: Catches hangs/deadlocks; misses logic errors that keep kicking

items.prompt: Summarize the current landscape of the commercial suborbital flight and microgravity research market, including the main categories of providers and the typical customer segments (research, technology de-risk, education). Public information only.

Draft a one-paragraph capability statement (public tone, no proprietary specifics) for a company that offers reusable suborbital flight test services to help other aerospace companies de-risk hardware before orbital deployment. Keep claims generic and defensible.
